source.title: Hej svenska 3 — study the theme before practising

status: Authored; two independent content checks required before merge.

lessons.scope: A country and its surroundings. Vilken goes with en nouns, vilket with ett nouns, and vilka with plurals.
Use har + supine for the perfect. A finished time such as i går normally takes the preterite. In a subordinate clause, inte comes before the finite verb.
Describe appearance and character. Eftersom introduces a reason. In that subordinate clause, sentence adverbs such as inte precede the finite verb.
Vill, ska, får, kan, behöver and måste are followed by an infinitive here, without att. Telephone phrases and imperatives practise making arrangements.
Practise employment words and workplace requests. Som introduces a relative clause; så att can introduce an intended result.
Compare adjectives with -are/-ast or irregular forms; use än for than. Purpose can be expressed with för att + infinitive.
Ingen, inget and inga agree with en, ett and plural nouns. Om introduces a condition; review definite plurals in housing contexts.
Use an auxiliary in short answers. Och adds, men contrasts and så can introduce a result. A subordinate clause placed first is followed by the main-clause finite verb.
The source labels this theme Tid, but its listed tasks concern personal finances. Distinguish låna (borrow) from låna ut (lend), and practise everyday money words.
Practise the language of appointments and symptoms. Också means too; heller is used with negation for not … either. These are language exercises, not medical instructions.
Practise relationships, compliments and replies. Att introduces a statement clause. Swedish adjective endings still agree with gender and number.
Practise civic vocabulary without memorising a changing list of parties. Både … och adds two things; varken … eller excludes both. Även om and trots att introduce subordinate clauses.
